items.text:
Hi everyone!

Installing skills globally in ~/.agents or ~/.claude consumes too much context, yet manually installing specific skills for every project is tedious. Wouldn't it be better to group skills for programming, backend architecture, or graphic design into collections, and install them with a single command only when needed?

To solve this, I built Skillset. It acts as a wrapper around the Vercel Skill CLI that batch-installs sets of skills from multiple sources using a single JSON file, essentially npm for skills!

While similar tools exist, most are written from scratch, which makes me concerned about their compatibility. Because Vercel’s Skill CLI is already the de facto standard (imo!), Skillset uses it directly as an underlying library. So it guarantees seamless compatibility across teams, regardless of whether they use Skillset or the standard Vercel CLI.

items.text:
rbit is a self hosted git forge designed around three core philosophies: speed, security, and efficiency.

We built rbit using Rust, Axum, Askama, Gitoxide, SQLite + redb, HTMX + Tailwind. Every piece of the stack was carefully considered to provide users with the fastest possible experience working with their repos without sacrificing the functionality you've come to expect from your existing git forge.

Our team is actively working to help make rbit the best it can be and we'd love to get your feedback while we continue improving!

rbit is built using rbit and it's CI/CD pipeline, we are dogfooding as we build it in the open. It has been localized into 9 languages including: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Russian, Chinese (Simplified), Japanese, and Korean. If you're a native speaker we would happily accept translation fixes!

items.text:
After my last trash clock (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49930439), I wanted to see how low I could go. My latest clock is built mainly from empty drink cartons, plus a few skewers, some paper straws, a piece of string, some nuts as weights, and lots of hot glue. It has a pendulum, an escapement, and hands for seconds, minutes, and hours, and runs for about an hour.

The design of the gears and escapement was AI-assisted: Claude built me interactive browser tools that generate templates and 3D-printable jigs and tools.

I’m happy to answer your questions! And to the commenter who suggested I submit trash clock timekeeping as a talk to 40C3: I did, and it got accepted. CU at Congress, I guess!?

items.text:
Hey HN readers!

I'm snipedbywifi (https://gitlab.com/snipedbywifi), and i've been working on terminactory. Please try it out if you'd like to play a cozy factory game while waiting for long agent tasks to finish!

The game is a factory game (overused niche, i know xD), but runs in your terminal. Reason i built it? glad you asked: So basically, it started off with me wanting a terminal-native factory game. Me and the modern 5.5 claude models made a base for the game that I liked, and then i went ham adding features / fixing some minor flaws (like adding claude code hooks so you recieve "telegrams" [the agent's responses], so you can review progress directly in-game). (yes, I had heavy AI assistance, disclaimer!!!)

Right now, the game has basic factory features you'd expect from a game like this (build stuff, delete stuff, measure how much you're earning, basic selection tools), along with a few more.. "unexpected" features. This includes a fake in-game browser that has a wiki, fake forums, some fun bits of lore, some more lore, a LOT more lore, and a research graph that shows how many items or how much RP (research points) you'd need to unlock something, and some more QOL features.

If anyone actually has this issue / want of a terminal-based game that runs alongside your agents so you don't doomscroll, do you have any suggestions, or additional ideas I could add?

It's hosted on GitLab, soo, that's one additional thing i'd like to mention

Thanks for reading!! snipedbywifi

(p.s. first HN post lol) (p.s. p.s. there's a lot of hidden lore in the game, so.. lore-divers? you might like it?)
